# Kagami

> Kagami is an open-source, deception-based defence against AI-driven attacks on web applications. It is an engine
> inside the app that detects attacks through tripwires only attackers touch (planted credentials, decoy routes,
> decoy fields, sealed IDs), misleads the attacking agent with decoys, and hands each detection to the developer's
> code through one callback, `onDetect(event)`. The developer decides the response. The engine is Rust compiled to
> WebAssembly and shared by every language. Express, Hono and any fetch app on Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare
> Workers are supported. It needs one self-generated secret, KAGAMI_SECRET, and no account.

Coding agents that are adding Kagami to an application should follow the integration guide step by step and finish
with `npx @agenticslabs/kagami doctor --json`.

## Integrate

- [Integration guide for AI coding agents](docs/ai/integrate.md): exact steps, checks and what to tell the owner
- [Getting started](docs/guides/getting-started.md): the same steps for people
- [Behind a proxy or CDN](docs/guides/behind-a-proxy.md): setting the client address correctly
- [Troubleshooting](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): every doctor result and its fix

- [How Kagami works](docs/guides/how-it-works.md): request lifecycle, tripwires, deception and the event
